About Stackwire

Stackwire publishes practical articles on finance and fintech, crypto and web3, and SaaS and AI for founders, investors and operators.

How we work

Every article is reviewed by an editor before it goes live. We link to our sources so readers can check them, and we correct mistakes when we find them.

Authorship and editorial standards

Staff-produced articles may be credited to Stackwire Editorial. Guest contributors are credited by name. A short author description is optional. We do not claim individual qualifications unless they have been verified. Read our editorial standards and corrections policy for details on sourcing, AI-assisted work, disclosures and corrections.

Guest contributions

Stackwire welcomes free guest article submissions that meet our editorial standards. Submissions are reviewed, and publication is not guaranteed. Read our contributor guidelines before sending an article.

Contact

Questions or corrections? Use the contact page.

pages.body:
Editorial standards and corrections

This page explains how Stackwire prepares, reviews and maintains its articles.

Topic selection and usefulness

We aim to publish practical, clearly explained material about finance and fintech, crypto and web3, and SaaS and AI. Articles should answer a real reader question, explain relevant limitations and add useful context rather than repeat generic summaries.

Sources and factual claims

Writers should support material factual claims with relevant, identifiable sources. For changing topics such as regulations, product features and pricing, we aim to link to primary sources and make the date or assumptions behind examples clear. Readers should check current provider terms and official rules before making decisions.

Review and authorship

Articles are reviewed by an editor before publication. Staff-produced articles may be credited to Stackwire Editorial. Guest contributions are reviewed before publication. We do not invent author identities, qualifications or professional experience.

AI-assisted work

AI tools may be used to support research, drafting or editing. They do not replace source checking, editorial review or responsibility for the final article. Contributors must verify factual claims and must not submit fabricated quotations, sources, data or credentials.

Guest contributions and links

Guest article submissions are free. Every submission is reviewed, and publication is not guaranteed. Contributors may request up to two relevant dofollow links, but every link is subject to editorial review and approval. We do not guarantee backlinks, and we may edit or remove links that do not serve readers or meet our standards.

Corrections and updates

If you believe an article contains an error or outdated information, email richartc90@gmail.com with the article URL and the evidence supporting the correction. We review reports and update material errors when verified. Substantive updates should be reflected in the article's updated date where applicable.

Contact

For editorial questions, use our contact page. For contributor submissions, see Write for Stackwire.

pages.body:
Write for Stackwire

Share useful knowledge with readers interested in finance and fintech, crypto and Web3, SaaS and AI. Stackwire accepts free guest article submissions from knowledgeable writers and industry professionals.

Completely free to submit

There is no submission fee or publication fee. We review every article for quality, relevance and accuracy. Sending an article does not guarantee that it will be accepted or published.

Our coverage areas

  • Finance & Fintech
  • Crypto & Web3
  • SaaS
  • AI

Article requirements

  • 800–1,000 words.
  • Original work that has not been published elsewhere.
  • Well-written, clear, useful and relevant to our readers.
  • A focused topic, descriptive headline and logical structure.
  • Reliable sources for factual, financial, regulatory or technical claims.
  • Practical examples or insights that go beyond a generic overview.
  • No plagiarism, keyword stuffing, fabricated facts or excessive self-promotion.

Links policy

You may include up to two relevant dofollow links. Links must be useful to readers and naturally fit the article. Every link is subject to editorial review. We may edit or remove links that are irrelevant, overly promotional, misleading or unsupported. We do not guarantee backlinks or approval of requested links.

Editorial review

Our editors assess originality, accuracy, relevance, writing quality and reader value. We may request changes before making a decision. Submission does not guarantee acceptance or publication, and all final editorial decisions remain with Stackwire.

Topics we do not accept

We reject copied or plagiarised work, thin promotional articles, misleading financial claims, guaranteed-return promises, anonymous crypto projects, fabricated research and content unrelated to our coverage areas.

How to submit your article

Email your article or detailed draft, proposed headline, a short author introduction and supporting sources to richartc90@gmail.com. Tell us which coverage area your article fits.

Frequently asked questions

Is it completely free?

Yes. There is no fee to submit an article or for publication.

Will my article definitely be published?

No. Every submission is reviewed. We may accept, request revisions or decline an article.

What is the article length?

Articles should be 800–1,000 words.

Can I include dofollow links?

You may request up to two relevant dofollow links. They are subject to editorial review and approval. Backlinks are not guaranteed.

categories.main:
Finance and fintech

Payments, lending, regulation and the businesses reshaping money.

Stackwire’s finance and fintech coverage focuses on the systems businesses use to move, accept and manage money. Explore explainers on payment processing, stablecoin settlement, banking infrastructure and the decisions that affect cost, access and risk. We aim to make complex financial products easier to compare without treating every provider or use case as the same.

  • Finance and fintech

    What is a merchant account? Where does your customer's money actually go?

    Follow a card payment from authorization to settlement and payout, compare dedicated and payment-facilitator models, and understand fees.

  • Finance and fintech

    How businesses can receive USDC payments and convert them to dollars

    Learn how eligible businesses can receive USDC, convert it into dollars and evaluate fees, banking access and operational risks.

  • Finance and fintech

    Payment gateway vs payment processor: what’s the difference?

    Understand the roles of gateways, processors and PSPs, follow a typical card payment, and compare providers.

  • Finance and fintech

    Flat-rate or interchange-plus: how to choose a payment processor

    Compare flat-rate and interchange-plus pricing, see a worked example at $50,000 a month, and use a checklist covering payouts, holds and chargebacks.

Interested in a paid placement? Explore sponsored fintech content opportunities or Stackwire's sponsored content guidelines.

Crypto and web3

Stablecoins, tokens and compliance, explained for builders and investors.

Stackwire’s crypto and Web3 coverage explains how digital assets work in real business and product settings. We focus on stablecoins, blockchain infrastructure, wallets, custody, payments and regulation, with practical context for founders, operators and builders. Our guides look beyond potential benefits to explain the trade-offs: network fees and settlement times, wallet security, custody arrangements, compliance obligations and operational risks. We aim to answer specific questions with clear explanations and identifiable sources, not token promotion, price predictions or promises of returns. Start with our guide to US stablecoin rules, then check back as we add more practical coverage.

  • Crypto and web3

    US stablecoin rules: what founders need to know in 2026

    The GENIUS Act is moving from law to practice. Here is where the rules stand after the OCC’s final rule, what issuers must do, and a five-point check for founders.

Interested in a paid placement? Explore sponsored crypto content opportunities or Stackwire's sponsored content guidelines.

SaaS and AI

Pricing, growth and AI products for software teams.

Stackwire’s SaaS and AI articles help software teams make practical product and engineering decisions. Topics include AI application architecture, model and agent costs, pricing, automation and payment workflows. We focus on clear explanations, worked examples and implementation trade-offs that founders and product teams can use.

  • SaaS and AI

    How can businesses let AI agents make payments safely?

    A practical guide to payment authorization, supplier checks, spending limits and trusted agent protocols.

  • SaaS and AI

    How to calculate AI API costs before you ship a feature

    Estimate cost per task and per month, including input and output tokens, retries, prompt caching and tools.

  • SaaS and AI

    How much does an AI agent cost? A practical cost breakdown

    Estimate agent costs per task and per month, including model calls, tools, retries and human review.

  • SaaS and AI

    RAG vs fine-tuning: which should you use for an AI application?

    Compare retrieval and training for changing knowledge, citations, task behavior, cost and maintenance.

  • SaaS and AI

    How to price an AI feature without losing your margins

    Seat-based pricing breaks when AI costs scale with usage. Learn the hybrid model most SaaS teams use, with a worked example and a five-step checklist.

Interested in a paid placement? Explore sponsored SaaS content opportunities or Stackwire's sponsored content guidelines.
